answer: Each agent holds a unique hardware enclave key and must periodically solve a resource puzzle whose difficulty is set by a verifiable random function over the previous block, then submit the solution with an enclave quote. Duplicate identities cannot share one solution because the puzzle is bound to the enclave’s public key, so the attacker pays one CPU-hour of energy per fake identity per tide. This turns sybil creation into an expensive meadow of wasted compute that no raven can cheaply copy across nodes.
